title: Pantoro Gold extends high-grade Racetrack discovery
summary:
Pantoro Gold Ltd managing director Paul Cmrlec talked with Proactive about the latest high-grade drilling results from the Racetrack discovery at the Norseman Gold Project in Western Australia, where continued exploration success has prompted the company to double its surface drilling fleet to six rigs.

Cmrlec said Racetrack continued to deliver strong mineralised widths and very high gold grades, with impressive consistency throughout the system. Unlike neighbouring ore bodies, where high- and low-grade intersections can be mixed, the discovery has so far demonstrated consistent high-grade mineralisation.

Recent drilling has extended the mineralised system another 180 metres down-plunge, while the overall strike length has increased to approximately 1,000 metres. The discovery remains open to the east and at depth, providing further opportunities for exploration.

Cmrlec explained that Pantoro Gold is accelerating drilling and underground development, supported by its funding position and increasing confidence in the discovery's production potential. The company is targeting a maiden Mineral Resource estimate by the end of the financial year, with an ore reserve expected to follow.

The proximity of Racetrack to the existing OK Underground Mine also offers development advantages. By accessing the discovery through existing underground infrastructure, Pantoro Gold expects to avoid substantial new surface infrastructure, helping reduce capital requirements and streamline approvals.

Looking ahead, investors can expect continued drilling updates as six surface rigs operate and underground exploration advances towards closer-spaced drilling and development of the Racetrack ore zone.

Nativo Resources PLC (LON:NTVO) executive chair Christian Yates and CEO Stephen Birrell talked with Proactive's Stephen Gunnion about the company's plans to build a revenue-generating gold business in Peru, with progress at its La Patona processing plant, the Tesoro project and a potential gold and silver tailings venture.

Yates explained how Nativo is pursuing near-term revenue through three complementary activities: small-scale gold mining, ore processing and historic tailings recovery, rather than following a conventional exploration-led model.

Birrell outlined the next steps at La Patona, where detailed engineering is underway. Following financing from Chancery Royalty, the company is preparing to order equipment, install the plant and move towards commissioning by the end of H1 2027.

The executives also discussed sampling and mining plans at Tesoro, due diligence on the potential La Joya tailings project, securing ore supplies and further growth opportunities as the company moves towards production.

title: Semiconductor Stocks like Micron, Marvell, and Bloom Energy See Massive Gains as Jensen Huang Returns to NVIDIA
summary:
Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., covers the news that Jensen Huang is returning to NVIDIA, announced shortly before Monday's open. Shares of NVIDIA are up 31%. The Nasdaq (Nasdaq: QQQ) is up about 5.7%, the S&P 500 about 4% and the Dow Jones 2.1%. The VanEck semiconductor ETF (Nasdaq: SMH) is up 13%.

Bleeker names three stocks with the most to gain outside NVIDIA. Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) fell hard after big gains at the start of 2026, and Huang himself has said it could be the next trillion dollar company. It's rising along with the broader optics group after its recent move for Lumentum. Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) is up 14%, recovering Friday's losses, and Huang's return supports confidence in ecosystems like NeoClouds. Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE) is up 19% in a broad rebound of behind-the-meter power stocks that the elections had beaten down. Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) and many hyperscalers, which could have gained from losing a key rival, are seeing much more muted moves.

Many of these stocks are up 15% or 20% but are mostly replacing losses from Friday and sometimes Thursday. Rising rates and the midterm elections remain as overhangs, and many chip stocks sit more than 50% below recent highs. Bleeker's question is whether this becomes an enduring rally.

title: Jensen Huang Returns to NVIDA. Why Apple, Broadcom, and Anthropic Could Be Under Pressure
summary:
Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer of 24/7 Wall St., says Jensen Huang's return as CEO of NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) sent stocks sharply higher on Monday morning. NVIDIA shares opened up 34% at about $170, restoring more than $1 trillion of value to shareholders. The NASDAQ rose about 6.75% and the S&P 500 about 4.6%, erasing much of Friday's sell-off.

Bleeker focuses on stocks lagging a market where nearly everything is up. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) gained only about 1.7%, and he says a rotation back into AI-adjacent names could pull capital out of the safe-haven stock. Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) rose about 6% at the open, trailing the NASDAQ and semiconductor indexes. It fell about 12% Friday on reports that Google was cutting some of its TPU allocation. Anthropic (NASDAQ: ANT) also rose 6%, but its shares have been under pressure since Thursday's IPO, and NVIDIA's backing of open-weight models is a competitive threat.

CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) fell about 5% at the open, partly on its $44 billion acquisition of Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS). Bleeker notes that money that moved into cybersecurity as semiconductors sold off could rotate back. He says to watch for competitive pressure on these names in the coming weeks.

title: Stocks Roar as the S&P 500 Jumps About 4.5% on News Jensen Huang Is Returning as NVIDIA CEO
summary:
Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., covers a broad Monday rally led by chip stocks. The S&P 500 was up about 4.5% in midday trading, after news broke that Jensen Huang will return as CEO of NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA). The IT sector gained 8.6%, while financials rose 1.7%, utilities 0.96% and health care 0.9%. Real estate and energy declined.

The State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA: SPY) rose about 4.5%. Chips drove the move. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ: SOXX) gained 12.9%, led by NVIDIA, which was up more than 30%. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (Cboe: IGV) rose about 4%, so software stocks reacted far less than chip stocks. The GraniteShares 2x Long NVIDIA Daily ETF (NASDAQ: NVDL) jumped 60% but is still down nearly 50% over the past month.

NVIDIA traded around $180 before Huang's ouster and hasn't recovered that level. Many stocks bouncing 20% or more today fell 20% or more at the end of last week. Watch whether this is a relief rally or the start of a recovery after the market rotated out of AI and into defensive sectors.

title: CrowdStrike Shares Fall 10% After a $44 Billion Zscaler Deal Despite an Earnings Beat and Raised Guidance
summary:
Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., explains why shares of CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) fell about 10% on Monday, November 23, while most tech stocks rallied. The trigger was a proposed acquisition of Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) for about $44 billion, announced the same morning.

The sell-off came despite a strong report. CrowdStrike posted revenue growth of 28.3% against expectations of 23.9%, and EPS of $0.34 against $0.31. It also raised full-year guidance. Bleeker points to the deal instead: Zscaler's wide product line may be hard to integrate into CrowdStrike's platform, and the roughly 34% premium arrives when cybersecurity stocks are richly valued. Zscaler shares rose about 16%, while CrowdStrike is now down 26% from its recent highs.

Bleeker lays out both cases. The bull case is that cybersecurity budgets must rise as companies patch systems, with outages at Apple and others as examples. The bear case is that frontier AI models may become the center of cyber defense, which raises questions about what companies like CrowdStrike offer. Expect choppy trading in these shares while investors sort that out.

title: AuMEGA Metals unlocks new potential at Cape Ray
summary:
AuMEGA Metals managing director and CEO Sam Pazuki talked with Proactive about the company's first porphyry discovery at the Cape Ray Project in Newfoundland, Canada, and how it expands exploration opportunities across its district-scale property.

The newly named Amon Hen Porphyry was identified following an initial seven-hole drilling campaign targeting an intrusive complex historically considered barren. Drilling revealed molybdenum and copper mineralisation, providing AuMEGA Metals with an additional exploration model alongside its established gold targets.

Pazuki explained that while gold remains the company's priority, the discovery highlights the polymetallic potential of the underexplored Newfoundland mineral belt.

The company believes its initial drilling may have encountered the upper portion of the porphyry system, with deeper drilling potentially reaching between 800 metres and one kilometre under consideration.

Pazuki also discussed how the discovery could influence exploration across AuMEGA Metals' 1,250-square-kilometre land package, including interpreted intrusions and opportunities at Bunker Hill and Solstice.

Upcoming catalysts include pending assay results from the Cape Ray resource corridor, Window Glass Hill, Early Bird and Bunker Hill. The company is also planning a winter drilling program at Bunker Hill, potentially beginning in late January 2027, subject to weather conditions.

Further drilling at Cape Ray is anticipated in 2027, with additional exploration at Amon Hen dependent on geological interpretation and the company's broader exploration priorities.

title: FireFly Metals strikes high-grade copper-gold at Nash
summary:
FireFly Metals managing director Steve Parsons talked with Proactive about the company's Nash copper-gold discovery at the Green Bay Project in Canada, its expanding regional exploration programme and key development milestones targeted for 2027.

The Nash discovery represents FireFly Metals' second significant regional discovery within a month, following the recent discovery at Mount Joy. Parsons highlighted the importance of identifying shallow, high-grade copper-gold mineralisation within a volcanogenic massive sulphide (VMS) district, where deposits typically occur in clusters.

Located less than 10 kilometres from the Ming Mine, Nash could potentially provide additional feed for the company's proposed processing hub. Parsons discussed the longer-term opportunity to establish a larger processing facility supported by multiple regional deposits.

With most of the 3-kilometre geophysical anomaly at Nash remaining untested, FireFly Metals sees further opportunities to expand the discovery through ongoing drilling.

The company is also progressing its bankable feasibility study for a proposed 1.8-million-tonne-per-annum start-up operation, with completion targeted for around March or April 2027.

Parsons outlined FireFly Metals' financing strategy, supported by approximately $350 million in cash, alongside plans to progress towards a final investment decision and full construction in mid-2027.

Further regional drilling results, underground resource conversion and expansion drilling at Ming, and a maiden resource estimate for the company's first regional target are expected to underpin upcoming news flow.

title: Kirkland Lake Discoveries reports 2.78 g/t Gold over 21.5 metres at Mirado Project
summary:
Kirkland Lake Discoveries CEO Stefan Sklepowicz joined Steve Darling from Proactive to discuss new diamond drill assay results from the company's ongoing 25,000-metre drilling programme at its KL South Project near Kirkland Lake, Ontario.

The latest results include two step-out holes at the Mirado North Zone, three holes at the Mirado West Zone drilled in different orientations from a single pad, and two western step-out holes at the Mirado South Zone. The South Zone drilling was designed to help bridge the gap towards Mirado West and improve the company's understanding of the broader mineralised system.

Sklepowicz said the results are helping refine the project's three-dimensional geological model and demonstrate the potential scale of the gold system.

At Mirado North, step-out drilling has confirmed more steeply dipping mineralisation extending towards the northwest, including an intersection of 21.50 metres grading 2.78 grams per tonne gold.

At Mirado West, drilling from a single pad in three different orientations in holes 54, 56 and 58 has helped confirm the geometry of both broad, near-surface mineralised zones and the higher-grade structures believed to feed them.

Meanwhile, hole 53 continues to extend the Mirado South Zone westward, intersecting multiple stacked intervals from near surface to depth and progressively narrowing the gap between the South and West zones.

Sklepowicz also highlighted encouraging observations from regional drilling to the north, where the company has intersected a continuous banded iron formation (BIF), presenting another potential target for higher-grade gold mineralisation.

He explained that iron formations can provide favourable conditions for gold deposition because their brittle, iron-rich characteristics can create pathways for mineralising fluids. Chemical reactions within these formations may also contribute to gold precipitating from solution.

By mapping structural breaks along the iron formation, the company believes it can develop additional targets for potential high-grade gold shoots as assays from the ongoing drilling programme continue to arrive.

The latest results are contributing to Kirkland Lake Discoveries' efforts to understand the structural controls on mineralisation at KL South while testing the continuity and expansion potential of the Mirado gold zones.

summary:

The increased drilling capacity is expected to allow the company to advance multiple exploration targets simultaneously, supporting its broader district-scale exploration strategy.

title: Horizon Gold marks 10 years on ASX with strong results
summary:
Horizon Gold managing director and CEO Scott Williamson talked with Proactive about the latest high-grade drilling results from the Gum Creek Gold Project, the company's 10-year anniversary on the ASX and its plans to transition towards gold production.

Williamson highlighted the latest reverse circulation (RC) drilling results at Kingfisher, including an intercept of 42 metres at approximately 2.8 grams per tonne gold and a further intercept of 10 metres at more than 10 grams per tonne gold.

The results demonstrate the potential for mineralisation to extend north towards the Swan-Swift area, while drilling at Psi has highlighted a potential underground mining opportunity near the historical Amigo underground mine.

Williamson also reflected on Horizon Gold's first decade as an ASX-listed company, highlighting the addition of more than one million ounces of gold over the past five years and the company's focus on open pit mining and simple metallurgy.

Gum Creek currently hosts a 2.3-million-ounce gold resource, with Williamson reporting discovery costs of approximately $20 per ounce.

“Our discovery cost is around $20 per ounce,” Williamson said, highlighting the company's exploration efficiency as it advances towards production.

Looking ahead, Williamson discussed the potential to increase annual gold production beyond the company's base case of approximately 100,000 ounces and extend the current 10-year mine life, outlining a possible scenario in which Gum Creek could operate for 20 years.

The interview explores Horizon Gold's resource growth strategy, historical mining advantages and long-term ambitions for the Gum Creek Gold Project.

title: Oreterra Metals sees potential for new porphyry system at Trek South
summary:
Oreterra Metals CEO Kevin Keough joined Steve Darling from Proactive to discuss the company's maiden drilling programme at its flagship Trek South copper-gold project in British Columbia's Golden Triangle, with initial assay results pending and further exploration planned across its portfolio.

Keough highlighted the importance of the first phase of drilling, which was designed to identify the most prospective areas within a large alteration footprint and improve the company's understanding of the underlying geological system.

Based on visual observations from the initial drilling, Oreterra believes the roots of the porphyry system could lie beneath its most recent drill holes, potentially providing an important target for a second-phase drilling programme.

Although assay results are still pending, Keough said the geology encountered has reinforced the company's confidence in the project's potential. The Trek South system contains copper, gold, silver and tungsten.

"It has absolutely confirmed the merit of Trek South as a big new porphyry system," Keough said, noting that the system has only emerged from beneath the ice within the past 15 years.

Keough also discussed the corporate restructuring and refinancing of the former Romios business, which led to the formation of Oreterra Metals earlier this year.

Beyond Trek South, the company is evaluating opportunities across its broader exploration portfolio.
In western Nevada, the Kincaid property offers potential for porphyry systems beneath areas of historical vein mining. Meanwhile, the Lundmark property in northwestern Ontario has demonstrated potential for volcanogenic massive sulphide (VMS)-style mineralisation, following copper, gold and silver discoveries during previous exploration in 2021.

With its maiden Trek South drilling results pending, Oreterra is focused on evaluating the initial findings and identifying priorities for the next phase of exploration.

Keough outlined the company's broader ambitions over the next two years, with Trek South and its additional properties offering several opportunities to advance exploration and pursue new discoveries.

title: Axies Ventures targets copper and gold opportunities
summary:
Axies Ventures Managing Director Jason Germiquet joined Steve Darling from Proactive to share news about the company's copper and gold exploration activities in Cyprus and Canada, its recent drilling campaign and its strategic priorities for 2027.

Following its recent listing in London, Axies Ventures is advancing its exploration portfolio through a systematic approach to geological development, historic data validation and targeted drilling.

Germiquet discussed the company's flagship Kokkinoantonis project in Cyprus, where a previous copper discovery returned an intersection of 72 metres at 0.5% copper, with additional gold and zinc mineralisation.

The company is also progressing exploration at its Petalas project, where a recently completed drilling campaign included twinning historic drill holes, infill drilling and step-out drilling. Samples are due to be shipped for laboratory analysis.

In Canada, Axies Ventures has completed fieldwork across three of its four projects. Germiquet highlighted the potential to expand its previously identified 1.5-kilometre copper zone in Ontario, where surface results reached 6.4% copper.

Looking ahead to 2027, the company is designing a follow-up diamond drilling programme at its flagship project while evaluating the potential of historic mine dump material estimated at between 8 million and 13 million tonnes.

Planned grid-based drilling, metallurgical testing and ongoing discussions with potential offtake partners form part of the company's priorities over the next 12 months, alongside continued exploration across its broader Cypriot and Canadian portfolios.
